title: TanStack Table V9 Beta: Tree-Shakable Features, TanStack Store State, and Lower Memory Usage
gist: TanStack Table's V9 beta reworks state management around TanStack Store and makes features opt-in and tree-shakable to cut bundle size and re-renders, while lead maintainer Kevin Van Cott candidly admits the multi-year rewrite was delayed by trying to fix every V8 complaint at once.

insights.claim: TanStack Table V9 makes previously always-bundled features opt-in, letting a minimal table start around 5kb while a full enterprise grid only pulls in sorting, filtering, and pagination code as those features are registered, versus V8 where every feature shipped together.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Teams evaluating table libraries could see meaningfully smaller client bundles for simple use cases, a tree-shaking edge over monolithic table libraries.
insights.quote: a small table can start at around 5kb and a full enterprise grid pulls in sorting, filtering, and pagination as needed
insights.locator: The headline change is that features are now opt in.

insights.claim: TypeScript enforces TanStack Table V9's opt-in feature model at the type level, so an API method like setSorting only exists on the table instance once the sorting feature has been explicitly registered.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Compile-time guardrails against depending on unregistered features should reduce runtime bugs during migration and integration.
insights.quote: an API such as setSorting only exists once its feature is registered.
insights.locator: The headline change is that features are now opt in.

insights.claim: TanStack Table V9 rebuilds state management on TanStack Store, replacing V8's getState() pattern with table.state, table.store, and per-slice atoms, and adds a table.Subscribe primitive so a component like a row-selection counter can re-render independently of other controls touching the same table instance.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Fine-grained subscriptions should cut unnecessary re-renders in large enterprise data grids, a real performance win for heavy-table apps.
insights.quote: A new table.Subscribe lets row selection changes re-render only the count that displays them, instead of every control that touches the table instance.
insights.locator: The other big shift is state.

insights.claim: TanStack Table V9 launches in beta with support across seven frontend targets: React, Preact, Angular, Solid, Vue, Svelte, and Lit.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Framework-agnostic reach makes TanStack Table a low-risk default for teams that may switch frameworks or run multi-framework design systems.
insights.locator: It is available for React, Preact, Angular, Solid, Vue, Svelte, and Lit.

insights.claim: Lead maintainer Kevin Van Cott says TanStack Table V9's state design was borrowed directly from TanStack Form and TanStack Store, and that the rewrite was forced specifically because V8's state patterns started breaking once React Compiler became stable.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: React Compiler's stabilization is now acting as an external forcing function pushing state-management libraries across the ecosystem toward fine-grained reactivity over ref/getState patterns.
insights.locator: Lead maintainer Kevin Van Cott says the design was borrowed directly from TanStack Form and Store

insights.claim: TanStack Table's lead maintainer Kevin Van Cott publicly admitted the V9 release has probably taken too long after a multi-year delay, and said trying to fix every V8 complaint at once in a single release was a big mistake he would not repeat.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: A governance lesson for open-source maintainers and dev-tool backers: bundling too many breaking changes into one big-bang release stalls delivery and risks community patience.
insights.locator: Van Cott has been unusually candid about the multi-year delay

insights.claim: On Medium, developer Ahmad Fiaz warned that TanStack Table V9's new atoms API is not a drop-in replacement for controlled state, and that this distinction matters for both Angular and React consumers of the library.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Teams planning to adopt V9 should budget real migration and testing time for state-handling code rather than treating it as a mechanical upgrade.
insights.quote: the new atoms API in v9 beta is not a drop-in replacement for controlled state, and the distinction matters in Angular and React apps alike.
insights.locator: Writing on Medium, Ahmad Fiaz cautioned

insights.claim: A recurring pre-V9 complaint from TanStack Table users, raised in a Reddit thread, was that as projects grew, developers ended up fighting the library's extensibility model instead of writing application code.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Extensibility friction was a real churn risk for TanStack Table versus more opinionated commercial grids; V9's clearer plugin model is a direct response.
insights.quote: instead of writing code I'm trying to hack this library.
insights.locator: seen in a Reddit thread where a developer described growing projects

insights.claim: On the r/reactjs V9 announcement thread, a user asked whether TanStack Table still lacked per-table state after building a custom useTable hook to work around global-only meta; maintainer Kevin Van Cott responded directly, pointing to a table and column meta feature and guide he had just shipped.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Shows the maintainer actively closing known extensibility gaps in near-real-time during the beta window, a positive signal for responsiveness ahead of general availability.
insights.quote: Am I seeing correctly that there is still no per-table meta and everything is still global :(
insights.locator: One exchange under the r/reactjs announcement thread

insights.claim: TanStack Table V9 offers a useLegacyTable hook that runs the V8-style API on top of the new V9 core, plus an importable stockFeatures bundle that restores V8's everything-included behavior at the cost of larger bundle size, while table markup itself remains unchanged.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Lowers switching cost and risk for V8 users, allowing incremental upgrades instead of a hard cutover, which should support faster adoption of V9.
insights.quote: importing stockFeatures restores the old everything-included behaviour at the cost of bundle size
insights.locator: Migration is designed to be gradual.

insights.claim: TanStack Table remains free and headless in V9, contrasting with commercial table products AG Grid and MUI X Data Grid, while higher-level wrappers such as Material React Table continue to build on top of it.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: TanStack Table's free/headless positioning keeps pricing pressure on commercial grid vendors and preserves its role as the substrate other UI libraries build on.
insights.locator: Compared with commercial options like AG Grid or MUI X Data Grid

insights.claim: V9 is currently in public beta and is explicitly positioned by the project as the foundation for TanStack Table's future releases, rather than a one-off version bump.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Signals a long-term commitment to the new architecture, so teams timing adoption should expect the beta's state model and opt-in features to persist rather than be reverted.
insights.locator: V9 is in beta now, positioned as the base for future releases.
